clauses.requirement: The ESA (electronic sub-assembly, e.g. the LED PCB/control electronics of the rear lamp) shall be subjected to the test requirements of UN R10 Annex 8 paragraph 4 for narrowband electromagnetic emissions, as specified in paragraphs 4.1 to 4.5 and Tables 1 and 2.
The ESA emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or on an open area test site (OATS).
Emission measurements of the ESA shall be performed with an average detector.

Measurements shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver using the parameters defined in Tables 1 and 2; spectrum analysers and FFT-based instruments meeting CISPR 16-1-1 may be used for conformity measurements; FFT-based instruments shall continuously record and evaluate the signal during the measurement time, and if used the minimum measurement time shall be 1 s per analysis frequency band (real-time mode) of the FFT instrument.

When using a spectrum analyser for the 30 to 1,000 MHz range with average detector, the resolution bandwidth (RBW at -3 dB) shall be 100/120 kHz and the minimum scan time 100 ms/MHz; if a spectrum analyser is used for peak measurements, the video bandwidth shall be at least three times the RBW.
When using a scanning receiver for the 30 to 1,000 MHz range with average detector, the bandwidth (BW at -6 dB) shall be 120 kHz, the maximum step size 60 kHz and the minimum dwell time 5 ms.

The Technical Service shall perform the test at the intervals specified in CISPR 12 throughout 30 to 1,000 MHz; alternatively, if the manufacturer provides measurement data for the whole band from a test laboratory accredited to the applicable parts of ISO 17025 and recognized by the Type Approval Authority, the Technical Service may divide the range into 14 bands (30-34, 34-45, 45-60, 60-80, 80-100, 100-130, 130-170, 170-225, 225-300, 300-400, 400-525, 525-700, 700-850 and 850-1,000 MHz) and test at the 14 frequencies with the highest emission levels in each band to confirm the ESA meets the Annex requirements; if the limit is exceeded, investigations shall ensure this is due to the ESA and not background radiation including broadband radiation from the ESA.

The maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarisation) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.
